summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; one WebSearch used). No values recorded; every empirical item is pending. Q1 (debt stock/composition): primary leads are the PDMO Public Debt Bulletin (FY2024/25 close), PDMO monthly debt statistics (Shrawan and Falgun 2082), MTDS 2024, FCGO Consolidated Financial Statements FY2022/23-FY2023/24, MoF Economic Surveys, the IMF 2026 Article IV/seventh ECF review DSA annex, IMF WEO GGXWDG_NGDP and World Bank IDS. A coverage bridge (PDMO central government -> general government -> DSA PPG -> IDS external) is designed for conflicts C-08/C-09, and every ratio will carry a coverage label. Q2 (debt-stabilising primary balance): parametric method using src/economic_model/fiscal.py with a composite effective rate that folds the foreign-currency share and depreciation into debt_stabilising_primary_balance, verified against debt_path, over a growth x interest x FX x contingent-shock grid tied to 01C, 20C, 20B and config assumptions A-TGT-04a..d. Q3 (contingent liabilities): a 12-item register (guarantees, NEA incl. PPAs, NOC, other SOEs, on-lending, PPP/IBN, subnational, arrears/multi-year commitments, disaster reconstruction, pensions, financial sector, DSA stress parameters) with items to verify. For 01C FT-03/U3: 13 thresholds are identified with documentary sources (LIC-DSF 2018 Guidance Note and 2024 Supplement, located by WebSearch; NNRFC borrowing limits; debt law; MTDS benchmarks; 03A reserve floor; MAC SRDSF for a post-graduation branch), all values pending. FT-03 is challenged because DSA thresholds apply to PV of PPG external debt, not total external debt.

assumptions.text: Debt-stabilising primary balance uses the composite effective rate i_eff = (1-s)*i_d + s*[(1+i_f)(1+eps)-1]; substituting i_eff into fiscal.debt_stabilising_primary_balance(d, i_eff, g_n) reproduces the one-period steady state of fiscal.debt_path (algebraic identity, not an empirical claim). A constant stock-flow adjustment sfa adds one-for-one: pb* = d(i_eff-g_n)/(1+g_n) + sfa.

Nominal-face-value debt ratios (PDMO, WEO) and present-value ratios (LIC-DSF) are different quantities; FT-03 threshold tests use PV ratios only when a PV series from the DSA or a documented discounting (DSF discount rate) is available; otherwise the test is reported as not computable rather than approximated.
Stocks are Nepal-FY-end (mid-July) unless the source is IDS (calendar year-end); ratios use same-FY nominal GDP of one stated NSO vintage.

Depreciation eps in debt dynamics is NPR against the external-debt currency basket, built from the 20B currency table and the NPR-INR peg identity; scenario FX cases reuse config/model_config.yaml A-TGT-04a..d labels rather than new numbers.

Contingent liabilities enter debt dynamics as sfa shocks (called guarantees, SOE bail-outs, disaster reconstruction) sized from the register once values exist; they are not added to the baseline debt stock.
Capital spending financed by borrowing is subject to execution shortfall (02B) and does not convert one-for-one to public capital; revenue gains from DRMS measures are not assumed (02A).

Coverage bridge ordering: PDMO central government -> + provincial/local borrowing -> = general government (compare WEO) -> + guaranteed SOE/other debt -> = PPG public debt (compare DSA coverage table); external subset compared with IDS PPG; IDS PNG, IMF credit (if outside PDMO) and short-term reported as residuals.

challenges.text: FT-03 pass criterion 'external debt/GDP stabilises below the DSA threshold' mixes concepts: LIC-DSF thresholds apply to the PRESENT VALUE of external PUBLIC AND PUBLICLY GUARANTEED debt (plus a PV total-public-debt benchmark), not to total external debt; a financing gap (I/Y - S/Y) maps to the current account and to total external liabilities incl. FDI and private debt. Suggest splitting FT-03 into FT-03a (PPG external PV/GDP, PV/exports, debt service/exports, debt service/revenue vs thresholds for Nepal's debt-carrying capacity), FT-03b (PV total public debt/GDP benchmark and domestic NNRFC/statutory borrowing limits), FT-03c (reserve cover, 03A). State the share of the gap assumed publicly financed, as an assumption.

U3 'for the entire horizon' should be tested per debt-carrying-capacity case: thresholds shift if the CI classification changes, and the LIC-DSF itself ceases to apply if Nepal moves to the MAC framework after IDA/PRGT graduation (20C). Treat framework switch as a scenario branch.

Please record (or confirm 02C records) the DSA coverage table, debt-carrying capacity and the threshold row applied, with page/table references, so FT-03 thresholds and the risk rating share one observation set; avoid duplicate observations of the same DSA ratio.

02C needs the reconciled currency-composition table (SDR look-through) with coverage stated as central-government external debt (PDMO) and PPG (IDS), same FY-end date, to parameterise foreign_share and the eps basket.

ppp_track_record should capture, per PDA/PPP project, whether the government provides guarantees, VGF, revenue/PPA backing or termination compensation, so that the contingent-liability register can size PPP exposure.
NEA PPA commitments (take-or-pay, USD-indexed tariffs) and NEA borrowings on-lent by government are fiscal contingent exposures; please share the PPA commitment profile when retrieved.
Bank holdings of government domestic debt and a banking-crisis contingent liability (per LIC-DSF financial-market shock) are needed; share holder split and system size when retrieved.
Add a watch conflict: nominal (face value) public debt ratios (PDMO/WEO) vs PV ratios (DSA) — definitional classification; not reconcilable without the DSF discount rate.

uncertainty: High. No primary document was retrieved, so the debt level, composition, effective rates and contingent exposures are all unknown in this round. Structural uncertainties: (i) coverage differences between PDMO, WEO, DSA and IDS (C-08/C-09) can change debt ratios materially and are not reconcilable without the DSA coverage table; (ii) face-value vs present-value measurement matters for concessional debt; (iii) FY-end vs calendar-year-end dates and exchange-rate valuation; (iv) contingent liabilities (NEA PPAs, NOC losses, PPP guarantees, pensions) may be undocumented, so the register may understate exposure; (v) forward interest cost depends on IDA/ADB graduation branches (20C) and the applicable framework (LIC-DSF vs MAC SRDSF); (vi) the 2024 Supplement may have revised guidance used by the 2026 DSA.

definitions.effective_interest_rate: Interest paid in FY t / stock at end FY t-1, separately domestic and external (NPR, excluding valuation changes).
definitions.concessional_share: Share of external debt meeting the grant-element definition used by the source (state definition).

coverage_bridge_PDMO_to_IMF.note: Every ratio will carry an explicit coverage label (A, C, F or G) per 00B's challenge.

debt_baseline.periods: FY2014/15-FY2024/25 annual; latest month FY2025/26 (Falgun 2082) as within-year reference

debt_stabilising_primary_balance.method: Parametric. (1) Composite effective rate i_eff = (1-s)*i_d + s*[(1+i_f)(1+eps)-1]. (2) pb* = fiscal.debt_stabilising_primary_balance(d0, i_eff, g_n) + sfa. (3) Verify by running fiscal.debt_path(DebtAssumptions(initial_debt_ratio=d0, foreign_share=s, domestic_rate=i_d, foreign_rate=i_f, nominal_growth=[g_n]*T, primary_balance=[pb*]*T, depreciation=[eps]*T, sfa=[sfa]*T)) and checking d_T = d0. (4) For time-varying paths, report the full debt_path under the proposed primary-balance path instead of a single pb*. (5) Pair with fiscal.interest_burden(d, i_eff, revenue_ratio) for the interest/revenue test.
